notes.text: A systematic audit of panel reasoning (every claim decided by proposer-critic agreement without arbiter review) found a class of shared misreads: tenses, quarterly-vs-annual figures, baselines, and invented referents. 17 verdicts were revised with editor approval. As a result, the Donald Trump SOTU 2026 headline moved from 'Largely False' to 'Mostly False' (102 of 150 decided claims false-leaning); the Joe Biden SOTU 2022 headline remains 'Largely True' and strengthened.

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (reasoning error): The claim states the US is a member 'along with 29 other nations,' which means 29 nations besides the US — totaling 30 members.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (quarterly-vs-annual/unit confusion): The panel committed a quarterly-vs-annual confusion (error class b): the 6.4%, 6.9%, and 7.0% figures in the evidence are annualized quarterly rates, not the full-year 2021 GDP growth figure.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (quarterly-vs-annual/unit confusion, invented referent): the panel conflated two different cost comparisons — the RAND 5-10x figure measures a different ratio than the one the claim states, so the evidence does not contradict the claim.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (baseline selection): 'before I took office' baselines to FY2020 (deficit ~$3.1T), not FY2019 ($984B); on that baseline the FY2022 deficit (~$1.3T) is indeed less than half — though the drop partly reflects expiring COVID-era spending.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (colloquial-recency falsification): Rounding 89% to 90% is a colloquial approximation, not a material misstatement — the same category as 'nearly 90%' or 'about 90%'.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (tense/temporal misread): The panel committed a tense/temporal misread: the claim was made on 2022-03-01 (during Biden's State of the Union address), announcing that additional tests could be ordered 'starting next week' (i.e., around 2022-03-07).
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (invented referent): The claim is a specific narrative statement about one individual (Heath) whose lungs and body were ravaged by cancer from burn pit exposure — it is not a general scientific claim about all veterans or all cancer types.
entries.source: agreed-verdict-audit-2026-07-21 (Severity-tier model, conf >= 0.8, approved by editor)

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (tense/temporal misread): The panel committed a tense/temporal misread: it cited evidence from after the utterance date (E2, E4 from April 2026; E1 from March 2026) showing the shutdown was 'eventually resolved' to rebut a present-tense claim made on 2026-02-24.

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (tense/temporal misread, reasoning error): the panel's own evidence supports the claimed event and timeline; the False verdict rested on a misreading of the cited item's dating.

entries.reason: Reasoning audit (colloquial-recency falsification): The panel's reasoning commits a colloquial-recency falsification error (class d): the payment was distributed in December 2025, roughly two months before the utterance date of February 24, 2026.
